title: Strict Stability and Strict Minimality of Regular Area-Minimizing Hypercones: A Quantitative Characterization
summary: Let $\mathbf{C}=\partial E\subset \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ be a regular area-minimizing hypercone. We first prove that $\mathbf{C}$ is simultaneously strictly stable and strictly minimizing if and only if there exists $c_\mathbf{C}>0$ such that \[ \operatorname{Per}(F;B_R)-\operatorname{Per}(E;B_R) \geq c_\mathbf{C} \int_{F\mathbin\triangle E} \frac{\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathbf{C})}{|x|^2}\,dx \] for every $R>0$ and finite-perimeter set $F$ with $F\mathbin\triangle E\Subset B_R$.
